To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1 → P QCD Pomeron vertex in the 1 / Nc limit is a sum of two contributions, one of which is a sum of conformal blocks of a conformal field theory with a central charge c = 2, the other one a sum of conformally invariant scalar products of two conformal blocks of the same theory, and that the conformal blocks can be computed using the classical string theory in the conformal limit.

the 1/N c limit of the QCD dipole framework at small x Bj is conformally invariant and that the 1 → 2 Pomeron vertices can be expressed analytically in terms of one loop integrals of conformal invariant functions.
the dipole picture of QCD at small-xBj is conformally invariant in the 1 / Nc limit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and the properties of conformal field theories at the classical limit.

the 1/N_c limit of QCD is conformal invariant in a certain sense.
the QCD dipole picture of high energy hadron-hadron interactions is conformally invariant in the 1 /N c limit, in a sense which we make precise.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1 → 2 and 1 → p Pomeron vertices are given by a conformally invariant expression in terms of the 1/N c expansion.
the QCD Pomeron is a classical conformal field theory in the 1 / Nc limit.

the QCD Pomeron in the dipole framework is described by conformally invariant amplitudes in the 1 → 2 channel, while it is described by conformal amplitudes in a 3 → 3 channel, in the 1/2 → p channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conformal symmetry of the dipole correlation functions, together with the Hilbert space construction, is sufficient for deriving the 1 → n dipole multiplicity distribution and the 1 → 3 Pomeron vertices.
the conformal invariance of the 1/N c limit of QCD is a very powerful tool to compute QCD observables in this limit.
the 1/N c expansion is a very powerful tool for the study of the small xBj regime in QCD.
